# `set_motion_detection`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Turn the motion detector on or off (firmware 9.75, 64-bit only).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / READ |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, handler @0xf0430 (64-bit build) |

New in firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0, 64-bit build only. Starts or stops the motion detector on its own, without the track-or-capture logic of the motion monitor. wide_cam true addresses the wide camera; the call is routed or refused depending on the process type. Refused with 524 while smart follow runs. Detection state members (width, height, exposure, points) exist; their types and the event that carries them are unresolved.

Side effects: Starts or stops the motion detector; starting requires a running preview stream.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_motion_detection"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | params must be an object (209 otherwise). [READ] |
| `params.enable` | boolean | yes | - | true starts detection, false stops it. Missing or wrong type 106. [READ] |
| `params.wide_cam` | boolean | no | - | Address the wide camera. Wrong type 106. Routing depends on process type (210 when this process cannot serve it). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 209 | params is not an object, or invalid detection arguments | `invalid argument` |
| 106 | enable or wide_cam is not a bool | `expected bool` |
| 210 | wide_cam routing not served by this process | `wrong process` |
| 524 | smart follow running, view mode not allowed (INFERRED), or object-track owner taken | `busy` |
| 268 | detection already running | `already running` |
| 300 | RTSP not running | `not ready` |
| 254 | stopping the track failed | `track stop failed` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A failed relay to the other camera is only logged. The unit of the internal first argument is unresolved.

## Example

Request, request - READ shape, not captured; values invented:

```json
{"id":86,"method":"set_motion_detection","params":{"enable":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_motion_detection","result":0,"code":0,"id":86}
```
